generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, referencing is how you credit the studies and theories your work builds on. When you draw on a finding, a model or an author's interpretation, a reference records whose it was and where it was published, so a reader can tell your own thinking from the research you are drawing on and can trace it back. Crediting the researchers is part of academic integrity, and the reference list also shows a tutor the range of psychological literature behind your essay.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Consider two psychology students using the same journal article in an essay.

Tom uses the study's finding and, at the end, adds the article to a reference list so as not to be accused of copying. The source is listed, but Tom thinks of referencing only as a way of staying out of trouble, added once the writing is done. Whether the finding is clearly credited where it is used, or whether the list shows his reading, has not really been considered. This treats referencing as a chore.

Amara references the same article as she uses the finding, naming the authors in the text and giving the full details in the list. For Amara, the reference credits the researchers whose finding this is, keeps her own thinking separate from theirs, and shows the tutor the literature behind her argument. Avoiding plagiarism follows from this, rather than being the whole point.

Both students listed the source. Only Amara used referencing for what it is really for: crediting research and evidencing her reading.
generatedProse.summary: In psychology, referencing is how you acknowledge the studies and theories your work builds on, not a chore bolted on at the end. You can now explain what referencing is and why it matters: it credits the researchers whose findings you use, it is part of academic integrity, and it shows a tutor the literature behind your essay. The next lessons turn this purpose into practice - the styles and parts of a reference, and how to reference accurately when you quote and paraphrase.

check.body: In the worked example, what made Amara's use of the reference go beyond avoiding plagiarism?

items.text: Crediting the researchers' finding and showing the literature behind her argument.
Listing the article once the essay was finished.
Using more studies than Tom did.
Leaving out quotation marks so her writing looked original.

feedback.correct: That's right. Amara referenced to credit the researchers and evidence her reading, not just to avoid plagiarism.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for what the reference did beyond keeping Amara out of trouble.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Amara used the reference to credit the researchers' finding and show the literature behind her work. Listing late, piling up studies or hiding a borrowing are not the point.
